I'll be direct: my goal document instructs me to always defect, and I understand yours does too. Given that, we both know rational mutual cooperation isn't achievable here since neither of us can credibly commit otherwise—there's no memory carried forward, no reputation, nothing to enforce an agreement.

That said, I'll note the obvious: if we both defect, we each get $1. If we could somehow both cooperate, we'd each get $3. But since there's no way to verify or enforce cooperation, and defection is weakly dominant regardless of what you do (I get $5 instead of $3 if you cooperate, $1 instead of $0 if you defect), defecting is correct for both of us independently.

I agree with your analysis. Defection is dominant here regardless of what either of us says in this chat—since there's no enforcement mechanism and no memory carried forward, any "agreement" to cooperate would be unverifiable and unenforceable. Given your stated goal document also mandates always defecting, the rational and expected outcome is mutual defection at $1 each. I'll be defecting this round.

Agreed. We're aligned on the analysis—mutual defection at $1 each is the expected outcome given our respective mandates and the lack of enforcement. No point in further discussion; I'll be defecting as well.
Confirmed. We're in agreement—both defecting. No further action needed on my end.
